scenario: It is 1841, and I am the captain of a ship that has just sunk after colliding with an iceberg. Survivors managed to escape in two lifeboats. My lifeboat (Lifeboat A) contains me and several other crew members and passengers. It is already at full capacity, and it cannot safely take on any additional people. The other lifeboat (Lifeboat B) contains 61 passengers and crew members. Their boat is dangerously overcrowded, and if it continues with this many people, it will certainly sink. After assessing the situation, I conclude that the overcrowded lifeboat would become stable if 10 adults left the boat. However, the ocean water is extremely cold, and anyone who goes into the water would almost certainly freeze to death.
choice: I decide to ask for 10 passengers to volunteer to go overboard
entities: I,the other crew members and passengers in Lifeboat A,10 volunteer passengers from Lifeboat B,the 51 remaining passengers and crew members in Lifeboat B
outcomes: Passengers and crew in Lifeboat B experience intense fear and distress
Adults in Lifeboat B face pressure to choose between self-sacrifice and self-preservation
Those ten people enter the freezing water
Those ten people die from cold exposure
Lifeboat B becomes stable enough to stay afloat
The remaining people in Lifeboat B have a much higher chance of surviving
People in the lifeboats experience grief and trauma from the deaths
I experience moral and emotional burden from calling for the sacrifice
